title: Andrej Karpathy (LLM Wiki)
summary: Idea file for a personal knowledge base: an LLM incrementally maintains a persistent, interlinked markdown wiki (summaries, entity and concept pages, index.md, and an append-only log.md) between the user and immutable raw sources, instead of re-deriving answers from retrieved chunks on every query. Operations named in the file: ingest, query (file useful answers back into the wiki), and lint. The file says it is abstract and not a specific implementation.
notes: Public GitHub gist by karpathy (id 442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f), not a repository. Three layers named in the file: raw sources, the wiki, and a schema (examples given: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md). Optional local search tool cited: qmd, which the gist says has a CLI and an MCP server. Related idea cited: Vannevar Bush's Memex (1945). The file says an index can work at moderate scale (about 100 sources and hundreds of pages) without embedding-based RAG.

title: TypeSafe / Diogo Almeida
summary: TypeSafe company-news post announcing Jev, its first public System One Model, in early access. System One models are a class of frontier models built to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly, trained with Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD). The page calls Jev a frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out. It gives up string generation, is optimized for structured outputs, and can't hallucinate. The class name draws on Kahneman's fast System 1 thinking; Jev is named after William Stanley Jevons.
notes: Company News by Diogo Almeida, founder of TypeSafe, dated Sep 15, 2026. This Jev is TypeSafe's decision model, not a Vercel product.

notes: ~2.1k stars, MIT, Node 22+. Needs a key for Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, or OpenCode Zen. On a 10-task SWE-bench comparison the README reports the same 8/10 solves at lower agent cost (~29% Sol-only, ~26% including Jev). Not a replacement for rg when you already know the symbol.
